title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document aggregates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, people-ops, finance, security, and engineering teams.

Key principles

- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required and review quarterly.
- Separation of duties: approval and execution should be separated for sensitive actions.
- Auditability: all changes and purchases must have a clear owner, approval record, and audit trail.
- Risk-based controls: stricter controls for customer-sensitive or regulated data.

1) Access and permissions

Purpose: define how employees request, approve, and review access to systems, clouds, and data.

Scope: applies to all corporate accounts, cloud consoles, production systems, data warehouses, and third-party services used for Redwood business.

Request and approval flow:

1. Submit request via Access Request form (People Ops Service Portal). Include justification, duration, and scope.
2. Manager approval required for non-admin requests. For admin or cloud-level access, manager + security review required.
3. Access is provisioned by IT/Platform with a ticket referencing the approval. Ticket must include an expiration date for temporary access.
4. Audit: all approvals captured in the IAM system and synced to the audit log (retention 3 years).

Access tiers and examples:

| Tier | Description | Examples | Approval required | Review cadence |
|------|-------------|----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Tier 1 | Basic corporate access | Slack, Okta, Google Workspace | Manager | Annual |
| Tier 2 | Developer tools and infra (non-prod) | GitHub repo access, dev cloud projects | Manager + Team lead | Quarterly |
| Tier 3 | Production systems & customer data | Production clusters, DBs with PII | Manager + Security | 90 days |
| Tier 4 | Admin or IAM privileges | Cloud admin, SRE admin | Manager + Security + Exec | 30 days |

Temporary access

- Temporary access must include an explicit end date and purpose.
- Maximum temporary access: 30 days unless extended with documented risk acceptance.
- Emergency access (break-glass): logged and requires retrospective approval within 48 hours.

Access reviews and deprovisioning

- Team leads run quarterly access reviews and reconcile active users to headcount.
- Offboarding: HR notifies IT within 4 hours of termination; accounts are disabled within 8 hours and fully revoked within 24 hours.

2) Change management

Purpose: ensure safe, auditable changes to production systems, infra, and model-serving configurations.

Change categories:

- Standard change: Low-risk, pre-approved changes (e.g., routine config updates) logged in the change calendar.
- Normal change: Requires RFC, peer review, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency change: For incidents; must follow incident process and have retrospective RCA.

Procedure for normal changes:

1. Submit RFC in the Change Management tracker with owner, rollback plan, test plan, and impact analysis.
2. Peer review by at least one engineer outside the owning team.
3. Security review for changes affecting authentication, encryption, or customer data.
4. Schedule in the change calendar; notify stakeholders 72 hours prior for customer-impacting work.
5. Execute during approved window; monitor metrics and rollback if SLO regressions observed.
6. Post-change report within 48 hours documenting outcome and any follow-up tasks.

Emergency changes

- Must be documented in the incident system and converted to an RFC within 5 business days.

3) Data management

Purpose: protect customer and internal data while enabling teams to use data for product and analytics.

Classification levels:

- Public: data intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company-internal, low-risk data.
- Confidential: business-sensitive but not customer PII.
- Restricted: customer PII, regulated data, or data requiring encryption and strict access controls.

Controls by classification:

- Storage: restricted data must be stored in encrypted buckets (AES-256) and access-controlled via IAM roles.
- Transit: TLS 1.2+ required for all external-facing services and internal service-to-service communication.
- Retention: default retention policies set in systems; exceptions must be documented and approved by Legal.
- Masking & anonymization: analytics teams should use pseudonymized datasets where feasible.

Data handling checklist for projects:

1. Identify classification for each dataset.
2. Define controls (encryption, access lists, retention).
3. Submit Data Handling checklist to Security for review.
4. Implement monitoring (access logs, anomaly detection).

Data breach & incident response

- Follow the Incident Response runbook: notify security@redwood-inference.com, contain, gather indicators, and escalate to execs for high-severity incidents.
- Legal and People Ops involved for customer-notification decisions.

4) Procurement and expenses

Purpose: provide a simple, auditable purchase and reimbursement process that enforces spend approvals and budget ownership.

Approval tiers (examples):

- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000 - $25,000: Department head approval.
- $25,000 - $250,000: Finance + Procurement manager approval.
- >$250,000: VP or C-level approval and legal review.

Procurement process for vendors and purchases:

1. Requestor creates a purchase requisition in the Procurement portal with justification, cost center, and preferred vendor.
2. Automated budget check runs; if within budget and tier, approval is routed accordingly.
3. Procurement or Finance issues PO and tracks delivery.
4. On invoice receipt, Finance matches invoice to PO and releases payment within standard terms (Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated).

Corporate card and expense reimbursements:

- Use company card for travel and approved vendor subscriptions when possible.
- Reimbursements require itemized receipts and completion of the Expense form within 30 days.
- Per diem and travel caps are listed in the Travel policy section.

5) Vendor management and third-party risk

Goals: ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and reliability expectations.

Vendor onboarding checklist:

1. Vendor assessment: complete security questionnaire (Auth0 risk assessment form) and verify SOC 2 or equivalent for vendors handling customer data.
2. Data flow map: document data the vendor will access and classification.
3. Contracting: Legal to review and include necessary DPA, SLAs, and indemnities.
4. Procurement to issue PO and register vendor in vendor registry.
5. Operational onboarding: access provisioning scoped and timeboxed.

Ongoing vendor reviews

- Critical vendors: quarterly performance and security reviews.
- Non-critical vendors: annual reviews.
- Offboarding: revoke all access and ensure data return or secure deletion per contract.

6) Travel policy (summary)

Purpose: provide clear guidelines for business travel, cost controls, and safety.

Booking and approval:

- All travel must be pre-approved in the Travel Request form with estimated cost and cost center.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Lodging: mid-range business hotels; special rates via corporate travel vendor where available.

Expense rules:

- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Meals: capped at $75/day per traveler in high-cost regions (ex. SF, London) unless pre-approved.
- Local transport: use rideshare or corporate car service; mileage reimbursed per IRS guidelines.

Duty of care:

- People Ops maintains traveler contact info and emergency procedures.
- For high-risk travel, security assessment required and extra approvals may be necessary.

7) Internal templates and links

The following templates are available in the People Ops templates library:

- Access Request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request
- Change RFC template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-rfc
- Data Handling checklist: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/data-checklist
- Purchase requisition template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/purchase-requisition
- Vendor onboarding checklist: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-onboarding
- Travel request & expense form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/travel-expense

Escalation & contacts

- People Ops (access & offboarding): people-ops@redwood-inference.com
- Security (data incidents & access reviews): security@redwood-inference.com
- Procurement & Finance (POs, invoices): procurement@redwood-inference.com

Governance and review cadence

- This document and associated templates are reviewed annually by People Ops, Security, and Finance.
- Major changes to approval tiers, data classification, or vendor policy require cross-functional sign-off and publication notes.

Appendix A - Quick checklists

Access request quick checklist:

- Justification provided
- Manager approved
- Expiration date set (if temporary)
- Ticket created and linked to request

Procurement quick checklist:

- Budget owner confirmed
- Required approvals captured
- PO created before purchase (unless card purchase approved)
- Vendor security & contract review completed for critical vendors

Change RFC quick checklist:

- Rollback plan included
- Test plan included
- Impact & SLOs defined
- Monitoring & post-change report owner identified

Document history

- 2026-03-04: Clarified access tiers and temporary access durations; updated vendor review cadence (Aisha Patel).
